Question: How did the viking's form of government differ from the other countries at the time?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends want to play a game together. Some of your friends decide that one person will be the boss and tell everyone what to do. That’s like what happened in some countries back then—there was a king or a leader who told everyone what to do.

But the Vikings were a little different! They didn’t have one big king or leader telling everyone what to do all the time. Instead, they had groups of strong men called chieftains. Each chieftain would lead a small group of people, like a family or a bunch of friends. They would talk together and decide things as a group, or the chieftain would help make decisions for his group.

So, while other countries often had one big boss for everybody, the Vikings had lots of little bosses for small groups. That’s how their way of making decisions was a little different!
